 | Analysis of 3Q26 Consolidated Results | Credicorp Ltd. Reports Financial and Operating Results for 3Q26 
 3Q26 ROE of 19.9%, supported by loan growth, healthy asset quality and diversified revenues; FY26 guidance of ~19.5% and the medium-term expectation of ~22% reaffirmed. 
 Loans up 14.8% YoY and the NPL ratio improved -91 bps to 3.9%; CoR was 2.0%, including additional El Niño provisions, reflecting the updated quarter-end El Niño assessment, while NPL coverage rose to 120.9%. 
 Core income reached a new quarterly high, up 18.0% YoY, with Risk-Adjusted NIM improving to 5.7% on margin expansion and transactional deposits growth. 
 Innovation Portfolio contributed 10.7% of Credicorp’s risk-adjusted revenues, while
 Yape’s contribution rose to 9.8% as monetization accelerated. 
 Efficiency improved -26 bps YoY to 45.4% in 9M26, reflecting operating leverage alongside continued strategic investment. 
Lima, Peru – November 9, 2026 – Credicorp Ltd. (“Credicorp” or “the Company”) (NYSE: BAP | BVL: BAP), the leading financial services holding company in Peru with a presence in Chile, Colombia, Bolivia, and Panama today reported its unaudited results for the three- and nine-months ended September 30, 2026. Financial results are expressed in Soles and are presented in accordance with IFRS. 
3Q26 OPERATING AND FINANCIAL HIGHLIGHTS 
 • Net income attributable to Credicorp reached S/1,929.4 million, up 11.0% YoY and down 2.6% QoQ, resulting in ROE of 19.9%, driven by accelerating loan growth, healthy asset quality and diversified revenue growth fueled by strong transactional activity and continued investment in digital capabilities.
 • Total loans measured in quarter-end balances increased 14.8% YoY (15.2% FX-neutral) and 4.2% QoQ (4.0% FX-neutral). YoY growth was led by BCP’s Retail Banking, particularly Consumer and SME-Pyme, followed by Wholesale Banking, and to a lesser extent Mibanco. QoQ expansion reflected growth in BCP’s same segments and at Mibanco, where disbursements reached a record high in September. 
 • Total Deposits increased 14.3% YoY (14.8% FX-neutral) but declined 0.6% QoQ (0.9% FX-neutral). YoY growth was supported mainly by low-cost deposits, which represented 73.2% of total deposits and 62.0% of the funding base. The sequential decline reflected the normalization of a temporary Wholesale demand deposit recorded at 2Q26-end and partial migration from demand to time deposits. 
 • Net Interest Income (NII) increased 17.7% YoY and 6.0% QoQ, primarily driven by loan growth at BCP and Mibanco, particularly in higher-yielding segments. Net Interest Margin (NIM) expanded 36 bps YoY to 6.9%, as the yield on interest-earning assets rose to 8.8% and growth in low-cost deposits reduced the funding cost to 2.2%.
 • Asset Qualit y continued to improve, with the NPL ratio declining -91 bps YoY and -15 bps QoQ to 3.9%. Performance registered stronger origination, monitoring and collections capabilities, particularly at BCP Stand-alone, reflecting positive payment behavior and healthy vintages.
 • Provisions increased 37.4% YoY and 13.3% QoQ, reflecting additional provisioning after the El Niño risk assessment evolved to a “Very Strong” base scenario at quarter-end, with a Cost of Risk standing at 2.0%. YoY, underlying provisions increased alongside loan growth at BCP and Mibanco, reflecting a greater contribution from higher-yielding portfolios. Cost of Risk stood at 2.0%, NPL coverage strengthened to 120.9%, while Risk-Adjusted NIM improved 13 bps to 5.7%.
 • Other Core Income increased 18.8% YoY and 3.2% QoQ, rising to 29.3% of total risk-adjusted income as Credicorp continues to diversify revenues. Growth was led by increases of 20.4% and 14.3% in fee income and FX gains, respectively. 
 • Insurance Underwriting Result declined 6.7% YoY, reflecting a tough comparison in Life’s D&S line following SISCO reserve releases in 3Q25, partially offset by stronger P&C results. QoQ, results increased 25.8% driven by higher

 • Yape further consolidated its position as Peru’s leading digital ecosystem, as deeper day-to-day engagement translated into continued monetization gains. MAU rose 9.8% YoY to 17.0 million, while transactions grew 35.1% YoY, averaging 71 per MAU per month. Revenue per MAU rose to S/11.9, nearly twice expenses per MAU of S/6.1, raising Yape’s contribution to Credicorp’s risk-adjusted revenues to 9.8%, from 6.4% in 3Q25. Meanwhile, loans nearly quadrupled YoY to S/2.3 billion, with lending representing 31% of Yape’s risk-adjusted revenues. 
 • Efficiency Ratio improved 26 bps YoY to 45.4% in 9M26, remaining within 2026 guidance. Operating expenses increased 13.6% YoY for the first nine months this year, mainly reflecting continued investment in BCP’s commercial, technology and risk-management capabilities, and higher variable compensation aligned with stronger results. Innovation portfolio expenses rose 32.5%, supporting continued growth in risk-adjusted revenues. 
 • Solid capital base, with IFRS CET1 ratios at 11.9% for BCP Stand-alone and 15.1% for Mibanco.

 | Analysis of 3Q26 Consolidated Results | Loans in Quarter-End Balances 
 Total loans (measured in quarter-end balance) expanded 4.2% QoQ and 14.8% YoY. 
 If we exclude the exchange rate effect, total loans rose 4.0% QoQ and 15.2% YoY. 
 QoQ growth was driven mainly by: (i) an uptick in loans in Consumer and SME-Pyme at BCP; (ii) an increase in short-term loan issuances in Wholesale Banking at BCP; and (iii) loan growth at Mibanco, with loan disbursement volumes reaching a record high in September. 
 YoY, the evolution was driven mainly by: (i) expansion in most Retail Banking segments at BCP; (ii) growth in short and long term lending in Wholesale Banking at BCP; and (iii) solid loan growth at Mibanco. 
 Deposits 
 The total deposit balance (measured in quarter-end balances) dropped 0.6% QoQ, but rose 14.3% YoY. 
 The QoQ decline mainly reflected the normalization of a temporary Wholesale deposit. YoY, growth was spurred by expansion in the balance for low-cost deposits, which represented 73.19% of total deposits at the end of September (+281 bps YoY). This evolution attests to the strength of our transactional proposition and our capacity to capture deposits in a high-liquidity environment. 
 At BCP, the Liquidity Coverage Ratio (RCL) in PEN at 30 days stood at 162.7% under regulatory standards and 142.3% by stricter internal standards. The LCR in USD at 30 days stood at 144.0% under regulatory standards and 110.5% under stricter internal standards. | ▲ |

 | Analysis of 3Q26 Consolidated Results | Net Interest Income (NII) and Margin (NIM) 
 QoQ, Net Interest Income (NII) increased 6.0%. This result was mainly driven by an increase in Income and Similar Interest, which rose on the back of an increase in interest on Loans after volumes ticked up at BCP and Mibanco. Growth in NII was partially offset by an increase in Interest and similar expenses, which grew alongside growth in time deposits. 
 YoY, NII increased 17.7%. This evolution was mainly triggered by an increase in Interest and similar income, which rose alongside an uptick in loans (through the same drivers seen QoQ). This uptick was partially offset by Interest and similar expenses, which ticked up on the back of growth in time deposits. In this context, NIM rose 36 bps YoY to stand at 6.93% at the end of 3Q26. 
 Portfolio Quality and Cost of Risk 
 Asset quality continued to evolve favorably, backed by improvements in the origination and heightened capacities for monitoring, collections and recovery. 
 QoQ, NPLs rose 0.4%, which was driven by loan growth at BCP Stand-alone’s retail portfolio and Mibanco. The latter was attenuated by the favorable evolution of Wholesale Banking at BCP Stand-alone. 
 YoY, the NPL portfolio dropped 7.0%. This evolution was attributable to BCP Stand-alone, which registered improvements in payment dynamics and better performance for recent vintages in Retail Banking. 
 In a context of solid loan growth, Credicorp’s NPL ratio dropped -15 bps QoQ to stand at 3.9%. 
 Provisions rose 13.3% QoQ and 37.4% YoY, partially driven by our risk assessment of the El Niño Phenomenon, with a “Very Strong” event becoming our base-case scenario at quarter-end. The Cost of Risk (CoR) for the period stood at 2.0%. 
 Underlying provisions were relatively stable QoQ, as higher provisions in BCP Retail Banking and Mibanco were offset by improved performance in BCP Wholesale Banking.

 Insurance Underwriting Result

 | Analysis of 3Q26 Consolidated Results | Efficiency 
 Operating expenses increased 13.6% for the first nine months of the year, fueled primarily by an increase in Administrative Expenses, and secondarily, an uptick in the Employee Salaries and Benefits line. Administrative Expenses increased mainly due to higher technology costs at BCP, reflecting greater cloud usage and other IT-related services as transaction volumes grew. Employee Salaries and Benefits increased as BCP continued to strengthen its technology, commercial and risk management capabilities, and due to higher variable compensation at BCP and Mibanco, in line with improved results. Expenses for our innovation portfolio increased 32.5%, supporting continued growth in risk-adjusted revenues. 
 Operating Income rose 14.3% YTD. In this context, the Efficiency Ratio stood at 45.4% for the first nine months of the year, in line with this year’s guidance. 
 Net earnings attributable to Credicorp 
 In 3Q26, net earnings attributable to Credicorp stood at S/1,929.4 million (-2.6% QoQ and +11.0% YoY), which translated into an ROE of 19.9% for the quarter. This evolution was backed by solid results in all our lines of business. For the first nine months of the year, Credicorp reported net attributable earnings of S/5,974.5 million (+11.9% YTD).  Shared capabilities in technology, data, analytics, artificial intelligence, and risk management constitute a competitive advantage to accelerate value creation at scale. These capabilities strengthen decision-making, enable more personalized customer experiences, generate productivity gains and accelerate innovation, supporting further monetization across the ecosystem. 
 4. Delivering Strong, Resilient Returns Across Economic Cycles 
 With decades of disciplined execution, Credicorp has demonstrated its capacity to generate value across economic cycles. The combination of market knowledge and leadership, business diversification, and ecosystem-based competitive advantages strengthen our resilience and supports a sustainable trajectory of profitable growth and long-term value creation.

 Credicorp’s innovation portfolio complements and expands the Group’s core businesses through scalable digital platforms and a disciplined investment strategy to create value. This portfolio diversifies revenue streams; broadens our value proposition; and establishes new avenues for growth by leveraging the ecosystem’s capacities and competitive advantages. 
 The portfolio invests in verticals with high potential for growth, including Neobanking, Services for SME-Pymes, Acquiring, InsurTech, WealthTech and Health, where we drive initiatives in different stages of maturity. The Innovation Committees governs the portfolio through a formal process to evaluate and prioritize initiatives with differentiated value propositions. These initiatives seek to generate relevant changes in the business model and/or present significant potential to generate exponential growth. This framework allows us to allot capital dynamically; conduct follow-up with defined milestones; and re-allot resources to opportunities with higher potential to create value. The initiatives advance through five stages of development: origination, incubation, product-market fit, acceleration and scaling. Once operating maturity is achieved, initiatives can graduate and integrate in the Group’s core businesses. 
 Initiatives can incubate within core businesses or be channeled through Krealo, our Corporate Venture Capital arm, which establishes outside-in innovation through strategic investments and acquisitions that strengthen and expand current and future lines of business. The portfolio is managed with explicit financial appetites, which consider an impact on ROE of 150 bps and 350 bps on the efficiency ratio. Additionally, in 3Q26, we reached our ambition of representing 10% of the Group’s risk-adjusted income. 
 Neobanking 
 Within the innovation portfolio, we created a Neobanking unit that integrates Yape, Yape Bolivia, Tenpo and iO under a common operating model. The value hypothesis behind this unit entails accelerating efforts to build a more integrated digital system by capturing shared capacities, products and data to capture efficiencies; develop synergies; and scale the value proposition over time in the most disciplined manner possible. Neobanking brings together scalable digital platforms with high potential for financial inclusion, monetization and regional expansion, which strengthens the Group’s long-term growth thesis.

 Scale and engagement strengthen Yape’s relevance in the day-to-day 
 Yape has consolidated its role as a platform for daily use with 17.0 million MAU at the end of 3Q26. Growth is increasingly fueled by deeper relations with users: transactions increased 35.1% YoY, outpacing the pace of growth of MAU (+9.8% YoY) by three-fold with solid feature adoption and satisfaction levels. 
 This recurrence is the base of this model: each interaction generates data on users’ habits and needs, which improves knowledge of the client and risk assessment while broadening financial product offerings. The opportunity remains significant: revenue-generating transactions per MAU increased to 7.7 (vs 6.2 in 3Q25), while credit penetration (MAUs with an active loan) continued to expand, reaching 18.7% (vs 9.9% in 3Q25). 
 Growing monetization and operating leverage 
 In 3Q26, monetization continues to strengthen, where growth in revenues (77.3% YoY) outpaced the increase reported for expenses (39.2% YoY), elevating operating leverage. The uptick in transactionality and in the contribution of loans lifted monthly revenue per MAU to nearly twice the level of monthly expenses per MAU (stable at ~S/6 over the past four quarters), while the proportion of revenue generating MAUs increased to 88% (vs 85% in 3Q25). This evolution strengthened our capacity to transform scale and recurrence into profitability, leading us to post a contribution of 9.8% to Credicorp’s risk-adjusted revenues (vs 6.4% in 3Q25). 
 Payments are the key driver of activation and client knowledge 
 In 3Q26, the Payments business represented 44% of Yape’s revenues. Growth was driven mainly by Bill, QR/POS and Checkout Payments, while emerging use cases such as remittances continued to gain traction and delivered strong growth. In Bill Payments, the number of transactions rose 39.1%, driven by higher average ticket sizes and stronger adoption across specific categories, such as education.
